title: IL HB3851: SCH CD-CYBER-BULLYING

obligations: Create, maintain, and implement a policy on bullying that meets the criteria in the definition of policy on bullying and file it with the State Board of Education (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).

Base the policy on the State Board of Education's template for a model bullying prevention policy under subsection (h) and include the criteria set forth in the definition of policy on bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).

Include in the policy or implementing procedure a process to investigate whether a reported act of bullying is within the permissible scope of the district's or school's jurisdiction and require that the district or school provide the victim with information regarding services available within the district and community, such as counseling, support services, and other programs (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
Make school personnel available for help with a bully or to make a report about bullying known to parents or legal guardians, students, and school personnel (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).

Every 2 years, conduct a review and re-evaluation of the policy and make any necessary and appropriate revisions, and no later than September 30 of the subject year, file the updated policy with the State Board of Education (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).

Collect, maintain, and submit to the State Board of Education non-identifiable data regarding verified allegations of bullying within the school district, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school, in an annual report due no later than August 15 of each year starting with the 2024-2025 school year through the 2030-2031 school year (Sec. 27-23.7(f)).
Ensure the policy includes procedures for promptly reporting bullying, including identifying staff email and telephone number and a procedure for anonymous reporting (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(3)).

Ensure the policy includes procedures for informing parents or guardians of all students involved in an alleged incident of bullying within 24 hours after the school's administration is made aware of the students' involvement (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(4)).

Ensure the policy includes procedures for promptly investigating and addressing reports of bullying, including completing the investigation within 10 school days, involving appropriate support personnel, notifying the principal or designee, and providing parents information and an opportunity to meet (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(5)).
Ensure the policy includes a statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation against any person who reports an act of bullying and consequences for reprisal or retaliation (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(7)).

Ensure the policy includes consequences and appropriate remedial actions for a person found to have falsely accused another of bullying as a means of retaliation or as a means of bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(8)).

Post the policy on the school's publicly accessible Internet website, include it in the student handbook, and distribute it annually to parents, guardians, students, and school personnel, including new employees when hired (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(10)).

Ensure the policy includes a policy evaluation process to assess outcomes and effectiveness and make the evaluation information available on the Internet website or otherwise provide it to administrators, board members, personnel, parents, guardians, and students (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(11)).

Ensure the policy requires all individual instances of bullying and all threats, suggestions, or instances of self-harm determined to be the result of bullying to be reported to parents or legal guardians (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(13)).
prohibitions: Bullying on the basis of actual or perceived race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, physical appearance, socioeconomic status, academic status, pregnancy, parenting status, homelessness, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, military status, sexual orientation, gender-related identity or expression, unfavorable discharge from military service, association with a person or group with one or more of the aforementioned actual or perceived characteristics, or any other distinguishing characteristic is prohibited in all school districts, charter schools, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary and secondary schools (Sec. 27-23.7(a)).

No student shall be subjected to bullying during any school-sponsored education program or activity; while in school, on school property, on school buses or other school vehicles, at designated school bus stops waiting for the school bus, or at school-sponsored or school-sanctioned events or activities; through the transmission of information from a school computer, school computer network, or other similar electronic school equipment; or through the transmission of information from a computer accessed at a nonschool-related location, activity, function, or program or from the use of technology or an electronic device not owned, leased, or used by a school district or school if the bullying causes a substantial disruption to the educational process or orderly operation of a school and a school administrator or teacher receives a report (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(1)-(4)).
Reprisal or retaliation against any person who reports an act of bullying is prohibited (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(7)).
Falsely accusing another of bullying as a means of retaliation or as a means of bullying is prohibited and must have consequences and appropriate remedial actions (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(8)).
reading.what_it_does: This Illinois law amends the School Code bullying prevention section to require school districts, charter schools, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary and secondary schools to adopt, implement, file, and periodically review comprehensive bullying prevention policies. It expands the definition of cyberbullying to include posting or distributing unauthorized digital replicas beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, and requires annual data reporting on verified bullying allegations. It also creates a grant fund and enforcement mechanisms through the State Board of Education.
reading.effective_date: July 1, 2026; the addition of unauthorized digital replica to cyberbullying applies beginning with the 2026-2027 school year.
key_definitions: Artificial intelligence: has the meaning given to that term in the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

Bullying: includes cyberbullying and means any severe or pervasive physical or verbal act or conduct, including communications made in writing or electronically, directed toward a student or students that has or can be reasonably predicted to have the effect of one or more of the following: placing the student or students in reasonable fear of harm to person or property; causing a substantially detrimental effect on physical or mental health; substantially interfering with academic performance; or substantially interfering with ability to participate in or benefit from services, activities, or privileges provided by a school. Bullying may take various forms including harassment, threats, intimidation, stalking, physical violence, sexual harassment, sexual violence, posting or distributing sexually explicit images, theft, public humiliation, destruction of property, or retaliation for asserting or alleging an act of bullying; this list is illustrative and non-exhaustive (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

Cyberbullying: bullying through the use of technology or any electronic communication, including without limitation any transfer of signs, signals, writing, images, sounds, data, or intelligence of any nature transmitted in whole or in part by a wire, radio, electromagnetic system, photoelectronic system, or photooptical system, including electronic mail, Internet communications, instant messages, or facsimile communications. Cyberbullying includes the creation of a webpage or weblog in which the creator assumes the identity of another person or the knowing impersonation of another person as the author of posted content or messages if the creation or impersonation creates any of the effects enumerated in the definition of bullying. Cyberbullying also includes the distribution by electronic means of a communication to more than one person or the posting of material on an electronic medium that may be accessed by one or more persons if the distribution or posting creates any of the effects enumerated in the definition of bullying. Beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, cyberbullying also includes the posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means if the posting or distribution creates any of the effects enumerated in the definition of bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
Digital replica: has the meaning given to that term in the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

Policy on bullying: a bullying prevention policy that meets the following criteria: (1) includes the bullying definition provided in this Section; (2) includes a statement that bullying is contrary to State law and the policy of the school district, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school and is consistent with subsection (a-5); (3) includes procedures for promptly reporting bullying, including identifying and providing the school email address if applicable and school telephone number for the staff person or persons responsible for receiving such reports and a procedure for anonymous reporting, but this shall not be construed to permit formal disciplinary action solely on the basis of an anonymous report; (4) consistent with federal and State laws and rules governing student privacy rights, includes procedures for informing parents or guardians of all students involved in the alleged incident of bullying within 24 hours after the school's administration is made aware of the students' involvement and discussing, as appropriate, the availability of social work services, counseling, school psychological services, other interventions, and restorative measures, with diligent efforts to notify using all contact information available or reasonably obtainable within the 24-hour period; (5) contains procedures for promptly investigating and addressing reports of bullying, including making all reasonable efforts to complete the investigation within 10 school days after the date the report was received, involving appropriate school support personnel and other staff with knowledge, experience, and training on bullying prevention, notifying the principal or school administrator or designee as soon as possible, and providing parents and guardians of the students who are parties to the investigation information about the investigation and an opportunity to meet with the principal or school administrator or designee to discuss the investigation, findings, and actions taken; (6) includes the interventions that can be taken to address bullying, which may include school social work services, restorative measures, social-emotional skill building, counseling, school psychological services, and community-based services; (7) includes a statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation against any person who reports an act of bullying and the consequences and appropriate remedial actions for a person who engages in reprisal or retaliation; (8) includes consequences and appropriate remedial actions for a person found to have falsely accused another of bullying as a means of retaliation or as a means of bullying; (9) is based on the engagement of a range of school stakeholders, including students and parents or guardians; (10) is posted on the school district's, charter school's, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school's existing, publicly accessible Internet website, is included in the student handbook, and, where applicable, posted where other policies, rules, and standards of conduct are currently posted in the school and provided periodically throughout the school year to students and faculty, and is distributed annually to parents, guardians, students, and school personnel, including new employees when hired; (11) as part of the process of reviewing and re-evaluating the policy under subsection (d), contains a policy evaluation process to assess the outcomes and effectiveness of the policy that includes factors such as the frequency of victimization, student, staff, and family observations of safety at a school, identification of areas of a school where bullying occurs, the types of bullying utilized, and bystander intervention or participation, and the information developed as a result of the policy evaluation must be made available on the Internet website of the school district, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school, or if an Internet website is not available, provided to school administrators, school board members, school personnel, parents, guardians, and students; (12) is consistent with the policies of the school board, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school; (13) requires all individual instances of bullying, as well as all threats, suggestions, or instances of self-harm determined to be the result of bullying, to be reported to the parents or legal guardians of those involved under the guidelines provided in paragraph (4) of this definition (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

Restorative measures: a continuum of school-based alternatives to exclusionary discipline, such as suspensions and expulsions, that are adapted to the particular needs of the school and community, contribute to maintaining school safety, protect the integrity of a positive and productive learning climate, teach students the personal and interpersonal skills they will need to be successful in school and society, serve to build and restore relationships among students, families, schools, and communities, reduce the likelihood of future disruption by balancing accountability with an understanding of students' behavioral health needs in order to keep students in school, and increase student accountability if the incident of bullying is based on religion, race, ethnicity, or any other category that is identified in the Illinois Human Rights Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

School personnel: persons employed by, on contract with, or who volunteer in a school district, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school, including without limitation school and school district administrators, teachers, school social workers, school counselors, school psychologists, school nurses, cafeteria workers, custodians, bus drivers, school resource officers, and security guards (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
Unauthorized digital replica: the use of a digital replica of an individual without the consent of the depicted individual (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
compliance_steps: Review and update the bullying prevention policy to include the statutory definition of bullying, including cyberbullying and the addition of unauthorized digital replicas beginning with the 2026-2027 school year (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

Ensure the policy meets all 13 criteria in the definition of policy on bullying, including reporting procedures, parent notification within 24 hours, investigation within 10 school days, prohibition of reprisal, consequences for false accusation, stakeholder engagement, posting and distribution, evaluation process, and reporting of self-harm threats (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
File the policy with the State Board of Education by September 30 of the subject year, and every 2 years review, re-evaluate, revise as necessary, and file the updated policy (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).

Implement the policy by making school personnel known, providing victims with information about services, investigating reports, notifying parents, and applying interventions and restorative measures (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).

Collect, maintain, and submit non-identifiable data on verified allegations of bullying annually by August 15 starting with the 2024-2025 school year through the 2030-2031 school year (Sec. 27-23.7(f)).
Ensure compliance with data reporting to remain eligible for grants from the Illinois Bullying and Cyberbullying Prevention Fund (Sec. 27-23.7(j)).

Post the policy on the school's publicly accessible Internet website, include it in the student handbook, and distribute it annually to parents, guardians, students, and school personnel, including new employees when hired (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(10)).
If using AI or digital replica technology, ensure policies and procedures address unauthorized digital replicas as cyberbullying and train personnel accordingly (Sec. 27-23.7(b), (d)).
who_it_applies_to: nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary and secondary schools
notable_exemptions: Nothing in this Section is intended to infringe upon any right to exercise free expression or the free exercise of religion or religiously based views protected under the First Amendment to the United States Constitution or under Section 3 of Article I of the Illinois Constitution (Sec. 27-23.7(a-5)).

Bullying through transmission from a nonschool computer applies only in cases in which a school administrator or teacher receives a report that bullying through this means has occurred and does not require a district or school to staff or monitor any nonschool-related activity, function, or program (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(4)).
Formal disciplinary action cannot be taken solely on the basis of an anonymous report (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(3)).
The list of bullying forms in the definition is illustrative and non-exhaustive (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
reading.penalties_and_enforcement: The State Board of Education monitors and provides technical support for implementation, reviews each filed policy to ensure it meets the requirements, and if a school district, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school fails to file a policy by September 30 of the subject year, the State Board must provide a written request for filing; if the school fails to file within 14 days of receipt, the State Board must publish notice of non-compliance on its website (Sec. 27-23.7(d)). Schools not in compliance with the data reporting requirements of subsection (f) are not eligible to receive a grant from the Illinois Bullying and Cyberbullying Prevention Fund (Sec. 27-23.7(j)). The State Board of Education adopts rules for notification of schools that fail to comply with data requirements (Sec. 27-23.7(f)). This Section does not create a private right of action, but it does not prevent a victim from seeking redress under any other available civil or criminal law (Sec. 27-23.7(e)). No fines or criminal penalties are stated in the text.
how_it_affects_ai_deployment: Beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, schools must treat posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means as cyberbullying if it creates bullying effects, so AI tools that generate digital replicas of students can trigger the school's bullying policy (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

Schools must update their bullying prevention policies to include the expanded cyberbullying definition covering unauthorized digital replicas and file the updated policy with the State Board of Education (Sec. 27-23.7(b), (d)).

If an AI system is used to create and distribute an unauthorized digital replica of a student, the school must investigate the report under its policy, notify parents or guardians within 24 hours, and complete the investigation within 10 school days (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(4), (5), (d)).
Schools must include verified allegations of cyberbullying involving unauthorized digital replicas in their annual non-identifiable data submissions to the State Board of Education (Sec. 27-23.7(f)).

Organizations deploying AI in schools should ensure their AI tools do not facilitate the creation or distribution of unauthorized digital replicas that could constitute bullying, because noncompliance with data reporting can make the school ineligible for grants from the Illinois Bullying and Cyberbullying Prevention Fund (Sec. 27-23.7(j)).

What it does

This Illinois law amends the School Code bullying prevention section to require school districts, charter schools, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary and secondary schools to adopt, implement, file, and periodically review comprehensive bullying prevention policies. It also creates a grant fund and enforcement mechanisms through the State Board of Education.

Who it applies to

  • school districts
  • charter schools
  • nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary and secondary schools
  • State Board of Education

Effective date

July 1, 2026; the addition of unauthorized digital replica to cyberbullying applies beginning with the 2026-2027 school year.

Cyberbullying also includes the distribution by electronic means of a communication to more than one person or the posting of material on an electronic medium that may be accessed by one or more persons if the distribution or posting creates any of the effects enumerated in the definition of bullying. Beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, cyberbullying also includes the posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means if the posting or distribution creates any of the effects enumerated in the definition of bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
  • Digital replica: has the meaning given to that term in the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
  • Policy on bullying: a bullying prevention policy that meets the following criteria: (1) includes the bullying definition provided in this Section; (2) includes a statement that bullying is contrary to State law and the policy of the school district, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school and is consistent with subsection (a-5); (3) includes procedures for promptly reporting bullying, including identifying and providing the school email address if applicable and school telephone number for the staff person or persons responsible for receiving such reports and a procedure for anonymous reporting, but this shall not be construed to permit formal disciplinary action solely on the basis of an anonymous report; (7) includes a statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation against any person who reports an act of bullying and the consequences and appropriate remedial actions for a person who engages in reprisal or retaliation; (8) includes consequences and appropriate remedial actions for a person found to have falsely accused another of bullying as a means of retaliation or as a means of bullying; (9) is based on the engagement of a range of school stakeholders, including students and parents or guardians; (10) is posted on the school district's, charter school's, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school's existing, publicly accessible Internet website, is included in the student handbook, and, where applicable, posted where other policies, rules, and standards of conduct are currently posted in the school and provided periodically throughout the school year to students and faculty, and is distributed annually to parents, guardians, students, and school personnel, including new employees when hired; Obligations

  • Create, maintain, and implement a policy on bullying that meets the criteria in the definition of policy on bullying and file it with the State Board of Education (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
  • Base the policy on the State Board of Education's template for a model bullying prevention policy under subsection (h) and include the criteria set forth in the definition of policy on bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
  • Include in the policy or implementing procedure a process to investigate whether a reported act of bullying is within the permissible scope of the district's or school's jurisdiction and require that the district or school provide the victim with information regarding services available within the district and community, such as counseling, support services, and other programs (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
  • Make school personnel available for help with a bully or to make a report about bullying known to parents or legal guardians, students, and school personnel (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
  • Every 2 years, conduct a review and re-evaluation of the policy and make any necessary and appropriate revisions, and no later than September 30 of the subject year, file the updated policy with the State Board of Education (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
  • Collect, maintain, and submit to the State Board of Education non-identifiable data regarding verified allegations of bullying within the school district, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school, in an annual report due no later than August 15 of each year starting with the 2024-2025 school year through the 2030-2031 school year (Sec. 27-23.7(f)).
  • Ensure the policy includes procedures for promptly reporting bullying, including identifying staff email and telephone number and a procedure for anonymous reporting (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(3)).
  • Ensure the policy includes procedures for informing parents or guardians of all students involved in an alleged incident of bullying within 24 hours after the school's administration is made aware of the students' involvement (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(4)).
  • Ensure the policy includes procedures for promptly investigating and addressing reports of bullying, including completing the investigation within 10 school days, involving appropriate support personnel, notifying the principal or designee, and providing parents information and an opportunity to meet (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(5)).
  • Ensure the policy includes a statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation against any person who reports an act of bullying and consequences for reprisal or retaliation (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(7)).

  • Ensure the policy includes a policy evaluation process to assess outcomes and effectiveness and make the evaluation information available on the Internet website or otherwise provide it to administrators, board members, personnel, parents, guardians, and students (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(11)).
  • Ensure the policy requires all individual instances of bullying and all threats, suggestions, or instances of self-harm determined to be the result of bullying to be reported to parents or legal guardians (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(13)).

Prohibitions

  • Bullying on the basis of actual or perceived race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, physical appearance, socioeconomic status, academic status, pregnancy, parenting status, homelessness, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, military status, sexual orientation, gender-related identity or expression, unfavorable discharge from military service, association with a person or group with one or more of the aforementioned actual or perceived characteristics, or any other distinguishing characteristic is prohibited in all school districts, charter schools, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary and secondary schools (Sec. 27-23.7(a)).
  • No student shall be subjected to bullying during any school-sponsored education program or activity; while in school, on school property, on school buses or other school vehicles, at designated school bus stops waiting for the school bus, or at school-sponsored or school-sanctioned events or activities; through the transmission of information from a school computer, school computer network, or other similar electronic school equipment; or through the transmission of information from a computer accessed at a nonschool-related location, activity, function, or program or from the use of technology or an electronic device not owned, leased, or used by a school district or school if the bullying causes a substantial disruption to the educational process or orderly operation of a school and a school administrator or teacher receives a report (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(1)-(4)).

Penalties and enforcement

Schools not in compliance with the data reporting requirements of subsection (f) are not eligible to receive a grant from the Illinois Bullying and Cyberbullying Prevention Fund (Sec. 27-23.7(j)). The State Board of Education adopts rules for notification of schools that fail to comply with data requirements (Sec. 27-23.7(f)). This Section does not create a private right of action, but it does not prevent a victim from seeking redress under any other available civil or criminal law (Sec. 27-23.7(e)). No fines or criminal penalties are stated in the text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • Beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, schools must treat posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means as cyberbullying if it creates bullying effects, so AI tools that generate digital replicas of students can trigger the school's bullying policy (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

  • Formal disciplinary action cannot be taken solely on the basis of an anonymous report (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(3)).
  • The list of bullying forms in the definition is illustrative and non-exhaustive (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

Compliance steps

  • Review and update the bullying prevention policy to include the statutory definition of bullying, including cyberbullying and the addition of unauthorized digital replicas beginning with the 2026-2027 school year (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
  • Ensure the policy meets all 13 criteria in the definition of policy on bullying, including reporting procedures, parent notification within 24 hours, investigation within 10 school days, prohibition of reprisal, consequences for false accusation, stakeholder engagement, posting and distribution, evaluation process, and reporting of self-harm threats (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
  • File the policy with the State Board of Education by September 30 of the subject year, and every 2 years review, re-evaluate, revise as necessary, and file the updated policy (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
  • Implement the policy by making school personnel known, providing victims with information about services, investigating reports, notifying parents, and applying interventions and restorative measures (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
  • Collect, maintain, and submit non-identifiable data on verified allegations of bullying annually by August 15 starting with the 2024-2025 school year through the 2030-2031 school year (Sec. 27-23.7(f)).
  • Ensure compliance with data reporting to remain eligible for grants from the Illinois Bullying and Cyberbullying Prevention Fund (Sec. 27-23.7(j)).
  • Post the policy on the school's publicly accessible Internet website, include it in the student handbook, and distribute it annually to parents, guardians, students, and school personnel, including new employees when hired (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(10)).
  • If using AI or digital replica technology, ensure policies and procedures address unauthorized digital replicas as cyberbullying and train personnel accordingly (Sec. 27-23.7(b), (d)).
